newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares up on end to year-end selling.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares up on end to year-end selling.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose for the third straight trading day on Wednesday as companies stopped selling for quick end-of-year profits.
As the end of the financial year on June 30 approached, companies had been cashing in their gains from a market which despite recent falls had risen 70 percent in 12 months.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index inched 1.22 points higher to close at 349.36 points. Turnover was about average at 44.16 million pounds ($13.0 million).

"The market will be a bit dry for a while. The blue chips are much more scarce now, compared to the abundant supplies last week as the companies realised some cash," said Sherif Cararah of brokers EFG-Hermes.
Despite the new mood, Misr International Bank/MIBank fell sharply, by 20.62 pounds to 598.70. "It had a rally last week and then corrected," said Cararah.
The other big-volume bank, Commercial International Bank/CIB, moved in the opposite direction, adding 0.85 to close the day at 71.95.
The flour mill sector had a marked downward trend. The most active, Upper Egypt Flour Mills lost 0.10 to 78.00 but South Cairo Flour Mills gained 0.65 to 65.65.
Cements were mixed in relkatively quiet trade. The most active, Egyptian Tora Portland rose 0.50 to 86.50.

Cararah said there was strong demand for a placement of 1.5 million shares in Arabian International Construction at a price of 67.00 pounds. The offer opened on Monday and will close at the end of business on Thursday.
"It has been superbly good," he said.

The index for openly traded firms rose to 475.89 from 474.01 points on Monday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms gained slightly to 259.07 from 258.23. The market had a holiday on Tuesday for the end of the financial year.
Of the 93 shares traded, 37 rose, 29 fell while 27 ended unchanged, the CMA said.
